extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political philosophy and jurisprudence
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Hobbesian criteria for what counts as Law, how Laws must be made known and interpreted, the role and required qualities of judges, divisions of law, and distinctions between sin/crime/rights. Useful for understanding standards that make rules authoritative and enforceable in a commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law is the Command of the Commonwealth (Sovereign)
rubrics_metrics.description: at the Command of the Common-wealth, is Law onely to those, that have means to take notice of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law binds only those who have the means to take notice of it; there is no law over 'naturall fooles, children, or mad-men' or brute beasts because they cannot make covenants or understand consequences. Authority of law rests in the sovereign's command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten laws obliging all are Laws of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: if it be a Law that obliges all the Subjects without exception, and is not written, nor otherwise published ... it is a Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such laws need no publishing or proclamation; they are agreeable to the reason of all men and exemplified by the maxim: 'Do not that to another, which thou thinkest unreasonable to be done by another to thy selfe.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten laws limited to a condition/particular also follow natural reason
rubrics_metrics.description: if it be a Law that obliges only some condition of men, or one particular man and be not written, nor published by word, then also it is a Law of Nature; and known by the same arguments, and signs...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the sovereign gives no written instructions (e.g., to a minister, judge, or ambassador) those persons must take the dictates of reason as their guide; these duties fall under 'Fidelity', a branch of natural justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-natural (positive) laws must be made known to those obliged
rubrics_metrics.description: it belongeth to the essence of all other Lawes, to be made known, to every man that shall be obliged to obey them, either by word, or writing, or some other act, known to proceed from the Soveraign Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The will of another cannot be understood except by his word/act; hence positive laws require publication in a manner the subject can take notice of (writing, proclamation, public acts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing is law where the legislator cannot be known
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor is it enough the Law be written, and published; but also that there be manifest signs, that it proceedeth from the will of the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private actors may publish false laws; therefore sufficient signs of authorship and authority (public registers, public counsels, public ministers, public seals) are required to verify that a rule is a law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification is testimony/record not the authority of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifyed, I say, not Authorised: for the Verification, is but the Testimony and Record; not the Authority of the law; which consisteth in the Command of the Soveraign only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official records and seals verify that a law was proclaimed but do not create the normative force—the sovereign's command does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's sentence verifies law of nature in individual cases
rubrics_metrics.description: the Sentence of the Judge, that by Commission hath Authority to take cognisance of such causes, is a sufficient Verification of the Law of Nature in that individuall case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge with proper commission can declare what the law of nature requires in a particular dispute; his sentence is the operative verification for the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals must consult public registers for written laws
rubrics_metrics.description: when the question is of injury, or crime, upon a written Law; every man by recourse to the Registers ... may (if he will) be sufficiently enformed, before he doe such injury, or commit the crime ... Nay he ought to doe so: for when a man doubts ... the doing is unlawfull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person can inform herself of a written law and fails to do so, committing the act is unlawful. Similarly, complaining before consulting applicable law indicates a vexatious disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public commissions and seals verify officials' authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To have seen his Commission, with the Publique Seale, and heard it read; or to have had the means to be informed of it, if a man would, is a sufficient Verification of his Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects are obliged to use their best endeavour to inform themselves of commissions and public acts that affect obedience to officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of the law depends on sovereign power; authentic interpretation is the legislator's meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: the Interpretation of all Lawes dependeth on the Authority Soveraign; and the Interpreters can be none but those, which the Soveraign ... shall appoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those authorized by the sovereign can give the authentic sense of a law; otherwise interpreters risk usurping legislative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: All laws, written and unwritten, require interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: All Laws, written, and unwritten, have need of Interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural law too is obscure to partial men; written laws have linguistic ambiguities—no law can be well understood without knowing the final causes (the legislator's ends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writers/commentators do not have authentic interpretive authority unless sovereign authorises them
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interpretation of the Lawes of Nature, in a Common-wealth, dependeth not on the books of Morall Philosophy. The Authority of writers, without the Authority of the Common-wealth, maketh not their opinions Law...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly commentaries, however true, are not law unless given force by sovereign authority; treatises are not substitutes for sovereign interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The ordinary judge's viva voce sentence is the authentic interpretation in each case
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interpretation of the Law of Nature, is the Sentence of the Judge constituted by the Soveraign Authority ... For in the act of Judicature, the Judge doth no more but consider, whither the demand of the party, be consonant to naturall reason, and Equity; and the Sentence he giveth, is therefore the Interpretation ... which is Law for that time, to the parties pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge's decision applies the law to the facts and holds normative force for the parties in that case because it is given by sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: A judge's sentence does not permanently bind other judges (precedent has limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sentence Of A Judge, Does Not Bind Him, Or Another Judge To Give Like Sentence In Like Cases Ever After ... No mans error becomes his own Law; nor obliges him to persist in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinate judges may err and later correct; past judgments do not automatically transform into immutable law, especially regarding laws of nature and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between the letter and the sentence (intention) of the law
rubrics_metrics.description: In written Lawes, men use to make a difference between the Letter, and the Sentence of the Law ... it is not the Letter, but the Intendment, or Meaning ... in which the nature of the Law consisteth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When literal wording is insufficient or leads to incommodities, judges must seek the legislator's intent, supply gaps via natural law, or defer judgment until proper authority clarifies intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges should avoid following literal words to unjust effect
rubrics_metrics.description: if the Word of the Law doe not fully authorise a reasonable Sentence, to supply it with the Law of Nature; or ... to respit Judgement till he have received more ample authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cases of forced dispossession or contradictory evidence should be resolved in light of intention/equity rather than a literal reading that condemns the innocent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required abilities in a good judge (interpreter of law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The things that make a good Judge, or good Interpreter of the Lawes, are, first A Right Understanding of that principall Law of Nature called Equity; Secondly, Contempt Of Unnecessary Riches, and Preferments. Thirdly, To Be Able In Judgement To Devest Himselfe Of All Feare, Anger, Hatred, Love, And Compassion. Fourthly, and lastly, Patience To Heare; Diligent Attention In Hearing; And Memory To Retain, Digest And Apply What He Hath Heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit evaluative checklist for judges: knowledge of equity, incorruptibility, impartiality (control of passions), patience, concentration, and memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of laws (seven sorts in Justinian tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Institutions of Justinian, we find seven sorts of Civill Lawes: 1. The Edicts, Constitutions, and Epistles Of The Prince ... 2. The Decrees Of The Whole People Of Rome ... 3. The Decrees Of The Common People ... 4. Senatus Consulta ... 5. The Edicts Of Praetors ... 6. Responsa Prudentum ... 7. Unwritten Customes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a taxonomy for classifying sources of civil law (royal edicts, popular decrees, senatorial orders, judicial edicts, jurists' responses, and customs) and maps them to analogous English forms (proclamations, Acts of Parliament, orders of the House of Commons, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into Natural and Positive Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Another division of Lawes, is into Naturall and Positive. Naturall are those which have been Lawes from all Eternity ... Positive, are those which have not been for Eternity; but have been made Lawes by the Will of those that have had the Soveraign Power ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural laws are eternal/moral virtues (justice, equity); positive laws are enactments of sovereigns and may be written or otherwise declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of positive laws: human vs divine; distributive vs penal
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Positive Lawes some are Humane, some Divine; And of Humane positive lawes, some are Distributive, some Penal. Distributive ... determine the Rights of the Subjects ... Penal are those, which declare, what Penalty shall be inflicted ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributive laws allocate rights and liberties; penal laws address ministers/officers responsible for punishment. Penal commands are addressed to executors not the delinquent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divine positive law: declaration and obedience within limits of natural law
rubrics_metrics.description: Divine Positive Lawes ... are those, which being the Commandements of God ... are declared for such, by those whom God hath authorised to declare them. ... I conclude therefore, that in all things not contrary to the Morall Law ... all Subjects are bound to obey that for divine Law, which is declared to be so, by the Lawes of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects may be bound to obey divine laws declared by authorized human agents so long as these declarations are not contrary to natural (moral) law; private claims of revelation are not infallible grounds for obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental laws defined by their role in sustaining the commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Fundamentall Law in every Common-wealth is that, which being taken away, the Common-wealth faileth, and is utterly dissolved ... such as is the power of War and Peace, of Judicature, of Election of Officers, and of doing whatsoever he shall think necessary for the Publique good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion to classify laws as fundamental (their removal dissolves the polity) versus non-fundamental (abrogation does not dissolve the commonwealth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Law and Right (lex vs jus)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Right is Liberty, namely that Liberty which the Civil Law leaves us: But Civill Law is an Obligation; and takes from us the Liberty which the Law of Nature gave us. Insomuch as Lex and Jus, are as different as Obligation and Liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminological standard: lex (law) is obligation imposed; jus (right) is the liberty retained under civil law. Useful when evaluating claims about entitlements vs duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Law and Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Likewise Lawes and Charters are taken promiscuously for the same thing. Yet Charters are Donations of the Soveraign; and not Lawes, but exemptions from Law. The phrase of a Law is Jubeo, Injungo ... the phrase of a Charter is Dedi, Concessi ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charters grant privileges/exemptions to particular persons/groups and are not general obligations; phrasing indicates the nature of the instrument (command vs grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sin defined broadly as transgression or contempt of the legislator
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sinne, is not onely a Transgression of a Law, but also any Contempt of the Legislator. ... may consist, not onely in the Commission of a Fact, or in the Speaking of Words by the Lawes forbidden, or in the Omission of what the Law commandeth, but also in the Intention, or purpose to transgresse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sin includes internal attitudes and intentions insofar as they amount to contempt; mere imaginary pleasure without resolve to act is not a sin under this account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime defined as a sin manifested by act or omission under civil law
rubrics_metrics.description: A Crime, is a sinne, consisting in the Committing (by Deed, or Word) of that which the Law forbiddeth, or the Omission of what it hath commanded. So that every Crime is a sinne; but not every sinne a Crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminality requires an outward manifestation that can be accused and judged; internal thoughts without outward signs are sins but not crimes in human courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where no civil law exists there is no crime (though sin remains)
rubrics_metrics.description: where Law ceaseth, Sinne ceaseth. ... Secondly, that the Civill Law ceasing, Crimes cease: for there being no other Law remaining, but that of Nature, there is no place for Accusation; every man being his own Judge ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of civil authority, moral wrongs persist but human criminal prosecution does not; when sovereign power ceases, individuals may resort to self-preservation rather than legal accusation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignorance of the law of nature excuses no man
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorance Of The Law Of Nature Excuseth No Man ... every man that hath attained to the use of Reason, is supposed to know, he ought not to do to another, what he would not have done to himselfe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural law is presumed known by reasonable agents; ignorance of natural law is not an excuse. (Author notes three kinds of ignorance: of the Law, of the Sovereign, and of the Penalty.)
